author: Jason Stys
summary: Persist and restore identity-bound bounded recovery outboxes with original times, TTL/capacity losses and publish-failure retention.
rationale: Turns reconnect demonstrations into reproducible cold-recovery workflows with explicit at-least-once limits.
limitations: Trusted cleartext checkpoints use explicit persistence; no fsync/crash-atomic, distributed exactly-once or fencing guarantee is made.
Copying a snapshot into separate fresh processes can replay messages more than once; callers must stop old publishers and use unique message IDs.
Count-bounded batches can exceed the checkpoint byte cap; export fails instead of silently truncating.

visualReview.method: Every rendered page individually viewed at readable original resolution

scope: Reviewed documentation editions of the cited source. Checksums identify bytes, not authorship. Historical measurements retain their own dates; integration CI must be checked separately.
